nodes.statement: The current local free-roaming dog population is not continuously enumerated by the periodic national survey system.
Taiwan estimates the national free-roaming dog population every two years using a photographic capture survey method; the 2024 estimate was 141,584 dogs.
Free-ranging dog abundance estimates can be biased when detection probability, individual identification, registration, or population closure assumptions are inadequately handled.
Photographic mark-recapture and capture-recapture methods can use repeated individual observations to estimate free-roaming dog abundance under explicit assumptions.
Talea is a street-survey system that records roaming animal sightings, characteristics, routes, survey areas, and geolocated observations.
Repeated sightings need reliable individual reconciliation before they can support individual-aware population estimation.
Geolocated sightings should be connected to a continuously updated local population-estimation workflow for operational targeting.
Immigration and replenishment can undermine fertility-control effects in an open free-roaming dog population.

In Shoushan, modelling indicated that maintaining female sterilization above 75 percent could theoretically control the dog population, while roughly 50 to 100 incoming dogs per year could severely disrupt the TNR effect.
Taiwan's 2026 community free-roaming dog management program prioritizes risk hotspots, female-dog source control, pet registration, sterilization, owner responsibility, and community participation.
Miaoli reported about 7,400 roaming dogs in 2025 and stated that intensified capture and inspection were still being outpaced by abandonment, free-roaming owned dogs, and reproduction.

provenance.publisher: Miaoli County Animal Protection and Health Inspection Office

nodes.statement: Intervention records should be connected to subsequent population, welfare, conflict, and ecological observations so management effects can be evaluated over time.

provenance.boundary: The source establishes periodic national estimation; the stronger local-continuous limitation is an inference from survey cadence and scope.
The method family can estimate abundance, but applicability depends on design and assumptions.
Talea provides structured street observations; this packet does not assert that Talea itself produces continuous population estimates.
Sightings are a candidate input; individual reconciliation capability is not established here.
Miaoli's statement supports replenishment pressure in practice but does not establish the Shoushan numerical immigration estimate.
The program addresses source-control mechanisms; this edge does not assert outcome effectiveness.
Open-population dynamics motivate follow-up measurement; this is a planning relation, not a causal claim about a particular intervention.
